skills.trigger: When evaluating a chest X-ray with multiple pulmonary nodules to determine the specific zonal distribution and morphological characteristics for differential diagnosis.
steps: Assess the vertical distribution of nodules by comparing density in the upper zones (above the anterior 2nd rib) versus the lower zones (below the hilum/diaphragm level).
Evaluate nodule margins (well-defined vs. ill-defined/spiculated) and check for internal calcification.

Correlate findings: Lower zone predominance with well-defined, non-calcified nodules suggests necrotizing sarcoid granulomatosis; upper zone predominance suggests tuberculosis; uniform distribution suggests typical sarcoidosis.
